notes: I always choose stability over risk, even when I know the risky path might be better
My friends say I overthink everything. They're not wrong.
I regret not taking that startup offer in 2022. They just got acquired for 200 million.
I value freedom more than money, but I keep choosing money anyway
I'm good at seeing all sides of a problem, which makes me a great advisor but a terrible decision-maker

simulate_request.decision: Should I have taken the startup offer in 2022?

universes.name: Universe A: The Risk-Taker
events: Year 1: Intense burnout from 80-hour weeks. Almost quit twice.
Year 2: Product-market fit achieved. Team grew from 8 to 40.
Year 3: Promoted to VP Engineering. Stock options vesting.
Year 4: Company acquired for $200M. Your equity: $4.2M.
Year 5: Starting own venture. Freedom finally achieved.
universes.strengths_amplified: Ambition finally unleashed. Risk tolerance grew from 0.3 to 0.7.
universes.weaknesses_triggered: Burnout nearly destroyed you. Overthinking caused analysis paralysis on key hires.

universes.name: Universe B: The Safe Path
events: Year 1: Comfortable. Predictable promotions. No surprises.
Year 2: Watched startup succeed from sidelines. Bitter.
Year 3: Got a raise. Still earning less than startup equity would be worth.
Year 4: Started side project. Too cautious to quit day job.
Year 5: Comfortable but regretful. Midlife crisis brewing.
universes.strengths_amplified: Analytical skills valued at Big Corp. Great advisor to junior engineers.
universes.weaknesses_triggered: Risk-aversion calcified into fear. Freedom value never realized.

universes.name: Universe C: The Negotiator
events: Year 1: Kept Big Corp salary, advised startup nights and weekends.
Year 2: Startup hit product-market fit. Your advisory equity: $800K.
Year 3: Quit Big Corp. Joined startup as CTO, remote-first culture.
Year 4: Built the company you always wanted. Work-life balance prioritized.
Year 5: Company profitable. You have both money AND freedom.
universes.strengths_amplified: Seeing all sides = perfect negotiator. Analytical = built data-driven culture.
universes.weaknesses_triggered: Overthinking made Year 1 exhausting. But you learned to delegate.

stress_test_request.idea: I want to build a local AI coaching platform that reads your diary and gives life advice
stress_test_request.context: Target audience: people who want AI life coaching but won't upload diaries to cloud

stress_test_response.vc_question: What's your TAM? Most people don't have 48GB GPUs. How do you scale beyond hobbyists?
stress_test_response.customer_question: I already pay $20/month for ChatGPT. Why should I pay more for a local version with fewer features?
stress_test_response.competitor_question: Anthropic's next Claude release includes 'personal memory' mode. We'll make it free. Your moat is zero.
stress_test_response.regulator_question: Mental health advice from unlicensed AI? Liability insurance? What if someone follows the advice and harms themselves?
stress_test_response.verdict: The privacy angle is strong but the unit economics are weak. You need either (1) a cloud-hosted version with E2E encryption, or (2) a B2B play selling to therapy practices who want AI-assisted sessions. Current idea = nice demo, unsustainable business.
